title: Dr. Katherine Roche:
format: 16:9 · 1920×1080 (client asked for longer researcher versions; same look as the approved short)
headline: A basic scientist who moved her lab to patient variants, what the GRIN families changed, and the NIH research hospital study.
story: Dr. Roche worked on glutamate receptors for 30 years. When genetics found patient variants in the proteins she studied, her lab pivoted almost entirely to them.
The GRIN community changed her research: it brings dollars and teaches her more. Drugs may be further along than you'd think, but still slow; gene correction is further out.
NIH's research hospital can now bring patients in under a research protocol. It's not a normal hospital. The families made that direction possible.
do: Open on the NIH fact with “A research hospital. No one pays.”
Keep bite 10: her own limits on the study.
Cover cuts with the named B-roll or a punch-in (4K source).
End on bite 11, hold her face 1 s.
dont: Don't open on “small progress is important” (the short's hook).
No free-care or sign-up framing. No address, phone or “how to sign up”.
Don't tell the other researchers' stories (Traynelis, Park, Penn).
Don't fill time. Only what's interesting.

rows.visual: On camera. Start on “NIH” at 11:06. Cut the pause 11:15–11:16.
rows.motion: Hook text 0:00–0:03: <q>A research hospital. No one pays.</q> No logo, no name plate, no fade.

voice.quote: So NIH has the largest clinical research hospital in the world. … No one pays. They don't even have a billing department.

rows.visual: On camera. Cover the cut at 01:50–01:53 (the repeat) with MVI_0079.MP4 00:01–00:04 (Dr. Roche on the panel).
rows.motion: Name plate at about 0:12, small, lower left: Dr. Katherine Roche / Senior Investigator, NIH/NINDS.

voice.quote: so I am a basic researcher. … But then there was this explosion in human genetics … And it turned out that some of these variants are in the proteins I had studied for decades.

rows.music: Warm, quiet bed under the voice.

voice.quote: And I started off being a very basic scientist and really have pivoted. Our lab almost entirely focuses our research on these rare variants that are found in patient populations.

rows.music: Warm, quiet bed under the voice.

rows.visual: MVI_3787.MP4 00:19–00:58: a large gathering, including children, seated in a conference room.
rows.motion: Captions. The transcript writes “grand disorders”: caption what she says (it sounds like “GRIN disorders”).

voice.quote: Half my lab studies one class of proteins … But there's no advocacy group. … The other half of lab study is GRIN disorders. And it's just the community is hugely important. It gets more research dollars. But also, you learn more.

rows.music: Warm, quiet bed under the voice.

rows.visual: On camera. Cover a cut with MVI_0070.MP4 00:04–00:11 (infographic, pink RESEARCH hexagon). Bites 6a and 6b stay together.

voice.quote: But really, families would also like to have anything that helps the symptoms. And so small progress is important. … So there's a lot of potential pharmacological interventions that are further along than you might imagine. … So there could be short-term therapies, which are still lengthy to come up with, that are more drug-based. And there may be others that actually correct the gene. But those are almost certainly further in the future.

rows.music: Warm, quiet bed under the voice.

rows.visual: MVI_3776.MP4 00:04–00:13: the panel, Dr. Roche second from the left.

voice.quote: I know that parents are frustrated that developing therapies are so slow. Science is slow. Publishing is slow. …

rows.music: Warm, quiet bed under the voice.

rows.visual: On camera. No NIH footage exists: stay on her face. Hide the 2 cuts with MVI_0089.MP4 00:00–00:03 (Dr. Roche at the podium). Do not replay the hook lines.
rows.motion: Captions. Bite 9: the transcript writes “green or green centers of excellence”; caption what she says.

voice.quote: That's all changed in the last few months. I'm now associated with the neurogenetics team at NINDS. … This isn't to compete with them or supplant it in any way. … It's not a normal hospital. … It's a research hospital. … So it's all research associated.

rows.music: Warm, quiet bed under the voice.

rows.visual: On camera. Her face. No B-roll on the last line. Hold 1 s.

voice.quote: So the direct interaction is incredibly important. And it's made it to where we've expanded our research to try to get tissue and samples from patients. And I don't think we would have ever dreamed to kind of go in that direction if we didn't have such a robust relationship with the GRIN families.
